gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Noto Sans Sinhala lays a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through every line, its curve endings keeping well clear of one another. Groovy's nearly closed letters make a funky counterpoint to those open curves.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Noto Sans Soyombo is a sans-serif with a sizable x-height, its curves leaving wide, unclosed mouths. But Groovy's nearly closed letters, loosely tracked and funky, make the opposite case.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Groovy draws everything with one nib, funky and friendly. Noto Sans Sundanese is a sans-serif with open-mouthed e crossbars and capitals barely taller than its lowercase, so it sits quietly beneath.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Chunky and cheerful, then suddenly spacious. Groovy handles the loud, uniformly thick outlines, while the plain sans Noto Sans Sunuwar lets its curves leave daylight and keeps its ascender stems short.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-syloti-na: Friendly from the first letter, Groovy keeps its c almost shut and its lowercase loosely tracked. But Noto Syloti Nagri is wrong here: Noto Sans Syloti Nagri, a sans-serif with short ascenders and an a that opens its lower bowl, does the quiet work.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Tight little slits meet glass-bulb bowls. Groovy's funky, near-closed letters lead, while Noto Sans Syriac, the plain sans following, opens into tall, rounded bowls and wide, easy s turns.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-syriac-ea: Friendly and funky, Groovy nearly closes its c. Stretched out, Noto Sans Syriac Eastern, the plain sans here, reads comfortably, its curve endings never crowding each other and tall lowercase standing clear of small caps.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-syriac-we: Friendly, with wire-bent s curves that never thin, Groovy nearly shuts its c. Noto Sans Syriac Western, the plain sans, holds its terminals far from the stroke and gives the heading's closed shapes an open counterweight.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Constant-width limbs and a nearly shut c: that is Groovy, funky and friendly. And down a full page of text, Noto Sans Tagalog, the plain sans, settles into a dense middle-band texture, its curves keeping generous gaps.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Noto Sans Tagbanwa is a sans of open curves and clear gaps, its lowercase filling most of the height. And since Groovy has no thick-thin pulse to carry the eye, extended text leans on those open curves.
